title: The reset law, not its mean, acquires the harmonic profile
statement: For fixed n, monotone working Y and exact uniform null-slot resets, old-target terminal law is Hypergeom(n+ell-1,A,Y+ell-1); inverse-profile expectation Phi_s is EXACT harmonic entry/reset value, target-monotone and uniformly comparable to (1+mu)^-s with square-comparability. It is not an inverse of the mean martingale. Actual three-part cohort/plateau and integrated kill hazard give alpha=m/((L+1)m+1), fixed moments/Green and sharp abstract power in exact one-step reference subclass. Incoming Phi_s controls actual-A kill output and stronger grade s+p with n^[-alpha p/(2p+m)], not f_s(initial A). Carried preservation uses explicit bounded deletion (n,Y,A)->(n-d,Y-d,A-d),d<=m; no population-small carried output. Fixed k-slot uniform-without-replacement resets with ell>=k give finite composition of auxiliary hypergeom laws by exact factorial moments, same exponent with changed constants. Biased reset, matching mean, worker returns, immigration/seeds, arbitrary output losses, physical-clock/signed/global transfer are excluded.

requires: Genuine non-double-counted allocated progress subgenerators, collateral safety, bounded adverse batch size and actual per-label predictable participation; regularity/nonexplosion for Dynkin localization.

Each theorem retains its own fixed-population or admissible immigration/pure-deletion seed contract, actual first-terminal stopping and output loss, frozen ordinary labels, exact trace clock and reward-weighted potential.

Uniform/null-slot reset and without-replacement sampling laws for exact carried profiles; a matching mean alone is insufficient. Abstract control converses require free nonnegative finite-rate intensities with no common upper bound.
